facts.text: South Butler is home to the South Butler Nostalgia Dragway, a 1/10‑mile strip that revived in 1977 and now hosts four classic drag races each year.
In 1853, Antoinette Brown Blackwell, the first woman ordained as a U.S. minister, preached in South Butler, marking a landmark moment in religious history.
The Butler Historical Preservation Society, founded in 1984, restored the historic South Butler Union Church and rehabilitated the old South Butler Schoolhouse.
South Butler’s main crossroads are Route 89, South Butler Road (CR 271), and South Butler‑Conquest Road (CR 275), anchoring the hamlet’s layout.
The Sylvester Willard Mansion, a historic Cayuga Museum of History site, sits in South Butler and showcases the town’s architectural heritage.
In 2024, a Patriot Burial Historical Marker honoring Revolutionary War veteran Ezekiel Scott was dedicated in South Butler, celebrating the town’s early American roots.
